audit.why: FAVOURED 4/10 against 49.87% over 752 games holds for lane specifically: Ziggs has no dash and one 20-second hop, so every lane stage is Irelia's; the near-even win rate comes from his side-lane and teamfight shelling, which the late rows already acknowledge.

audit.why: Two different builds on one page, and the spike that decides when to commit gave the reader no number.
audit.corrected: spikes[2] rewritten to 'first item' with the 850-range Bouncing Bomb and Satchel Charge named; Satchel Charge's 20s and Hexplosive Minefield's flat 16s written into the cooldown and mid fields.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mines were called 'his passive minefield charges' and 'his passive mines' in early and mid. They are Hexplosive Minefield (E). Short Fuse (P), his actual passive, was never mentioned — and it is an auto-attack empowerment whose cooldown drops every time he casts.
audit.why: The packet flags this matchup as never naming a single Ziggs ability; the passive/E mix-up is the concrete instance.
audit.corrected: Hexplosive Minefield named with its flat 16s and slow in early and mid; Short Fuse named in phases[0].why and phases[1].why as the magic-damage auto that charges off his casts.

audit.why: It is the field that carries real cooldowns.

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. Check it before every step-up. - W Defiant Dance is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Satchel Charge (W) is 20s at rank 1 and 12s at rank 5 — it knocks him away as well as you, so he is catchable only while it is down. - Hexplosive Minefield (E) is a flat 16s and slows: cross it at an angle, not head-on.

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.
edits.after: Bladesurge (Q) and Flawless Duet (E) each stack the passive; arrive at four before you touch him, or bonus on-hit damage never funds the kill.

edits.before: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: Every low minion is a Bladesurge charge; shove them away and you must walk 850 units through his bombs.

edits.before: Ziggs spends Satchel Charge early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Satchel Charge spent on the wave leaves him a full 20 seconds with no hop at all.

edits.before: Ziggs wins by landing Satchel Charge, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Ziggs wins by hopping out of your stun with Satchel Charge, mining the ground you need, and poking from 850.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry by hunting him between hops: Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1, and nothing else in his kit moves him.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Ziggs's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, take the short lane: fight him in river and jungle where Satchel Charge cannot hop him anywhere useful.

edits.before: Q the low minions and keep the blade moving — your level 1 reset dance already out-trades careless mages.
edits.after: Q the low minions and keep the blade moving — Short Fuse charges faster every time he casts a bomb.

edits.before: W joins: the channel shreds incoming damage — hold it for his trade spell, not his autos.
edits.after: W joins: Defiant Dance cuts physical damage, but Short Fuse is magic — dodge, don't tank.

edits.before: Once you have Trinity/Black Cleaver your all-in speed crosses his bomb-spam range fast enough that he can't kite you out even with W hop resets.
edits.after: Once your first item lands, your all-in crosses his 850-range Bouncing Bomb spam fast enough that Satchel Charge cannot hop him clear.

edits.before: You dominate this matchup from level 1 through 6 because Ziggs has zero dash or blink to escape your Q-E-W all-in, and once you're in range his only answer is a short W hop that doesn't create enough distance. Walk up through minions to soak his bomb poke before committing your engage, since a clean Q dash into his face usually ends the fight in your favor outright. His passive minefield charges can punish careless positioning, so approach at an angle rather than in a straight line. Even at level 6, his ult is a slow skillshot combo starter, not an escape, so it doesn't change your all-in timing.
edits.after: You dominate this matchup from level 1 through 6 because Ziggs has zero dash or blink to escape your Q-E-W all-in, and once you're in range his only answer is Satchel Charge, a hop that does not create enough distance. Walk up through minions to soak his bomb poke before committing your engage, since a clean Q dash into his face usually ends the fight in your favor outright. Hexplosive Minefield slows on contact and is a flat 16s, so cross it at an angle rather than walking the straight line through it. Even at level 6, his ult is a slow skillshot combo starter, not an escape, so it doesn't change your all-in timing.

edits.before: Levels 6 through 11 stay firmly in your favor since Ziggs's Ultimate is built for burst damage and zone control, not disengage, meaning your dash-reset chain still closes on him just as easily as before 6. Keep punishing his farm patterns by all-inning the moment he uses W to reposition on minions, since that's his only mobility tool and it's now on cooldown. Roam timing favors you too: he has no wave-clear speed advantage over your Q resets, so you can hit side lanes faster than he can followup. Play a little wider around his passive mines late in this window since stacked charges can slow you mid-engage.
edits.after: Levels 6 through 11 stay firmly in your favor since Ziggs's Ultimate is built for burst damage and zone control, not disengage, meaning your dash-reset chain still closes on him just as easily as before 6. Keep punishing his farm patterns by all-inning the moment he spends Satchel Charge on the wave, since it is his only mobility and it is 20s down at rank 1. Roam timing favors you too: he has no wave-clear speed advantage over your Q resets, so you can hit side lanes faster than he can followup. Play a little wider around Hexplosive Minefield in this window, since its slow is what turns your dash-in into a walk.

notes: MC_REAL_GAMES reads 752 games, so this matchup was audited despite the near-even win rate. Level chart is Irelia 7/7 and both layers agree — no chart edits. The kit file carries a 'percentHealth' derived flag on Satchel Charge and the missing-interactions list turns that into 'bypasses stacking resistances'; Riot's own description of Satchel Charge says nothing about percent health or resistance bypass, so no claim about armour/MR being the wrong answer was written anywhere. Flag looks like a tooltip-parsing misfire.
